array-intersection.baseline: Use membership scans and suppress duplicate output.
array-intersection.contract: Return unique common integer values in any order. The guide's sorted-input variant additionally guarantees both inputs are sorted.
array-intersection.correctness: Both Chapter2 set forms are correct; examples are printed and cover repeated, disjoint and equal inputs, but not empty. Neither the unsorted guide alias nor the sorted-pointer guide variant exists at HEAD.
array-intersection.optimized: Hash only the shorter unsorted input; for sorted inputs, use pointers and skip duplicate matches.

baseball-game.baseline: Play commands forward on an active-score stack, then sum the surviving scores.
baseball-game.contract: Given a valid log of integer tokens and operations C (cancel last), D (double last), and + (sum last two), return the total of scores still on the record. Commands are guaranteed to have sufficient history.
baseball-game.correctness: The single archived list-stack implementation handles valid operations, including negative scores and cancellation to empty. Underflow is outside the contract and would raise IndexError. Printed comparisons cover mixed commands, total cancellation, a singleton and addition; there are no assertions or invalid-command tests.
baseball-game.optimized: O(n) stack operations and O(n) auxiliary score slots for a read-only log. Without a fixed-width score guarantee, repeated doubling can take quadratic total bits and bit work. A running total avoids a final summation but needs the same score history; buffer reuse changes the input contract. Review only: no worthwhile three-way comparison.
baseball-game.python: list.append, list.pop and sum are already the natural Python solution. A dispatch table or a deque substitution does not materially change the algorithm.

binary-search.contract: For a strictly increasing list, return the zero-based target index or -1. An empty list also returns -1.
binary-search.correctness: The original inclusive-bound search handles first, last, missing, and empty cases. It does not specify which duplicate to return.
binary-search.python: No list.index or bisect example is implemented.

character-replacement.baseline: Restart counts at each possible start and stop when that candidate can no longer be repaired: expected O(n^2) time, O(d) auxiliary space.
character-replacement.contract: Return the longest contiguous length that can become all one character with at most k replacements (k >= 0); characters are case-sensitive.
character-replacement.correctness: PASS for the length-only contract. Historical max_freq may overestimate the current live maximum after shrink; that cannot create a new infeasible record length, but the current window need not be a valid witness. The archived dictionary retains zero counts, so space tracks all distinct characters seen, not just live contents. Five assertions cover mixed letters, all same, empty, zero budget and distinct letters. The guide path aliases this tracked source.
character-replacement.optimized: Keep a nondecreasing historical count when only maximum length is requested: expected O(n) time, O(d) auxiliary space.
character-replacement.python: Use Counter.most_common to shrink with the exact current maximum: expected O(n*d) time, O(d) auxiliary space.

concatenated-words.baseline: For every start, count all B word blocks anew: O(B*w + n*B*w) expected time, O(d*w) auxiliary space.
concatenated-words.contract: Match every occurrence of the supplied equal, positive-width words consecutively, in any order and without gaps; return zero-based starts, in any order. Overlapping matches count. Empty word input has no matches.
concatenated-words.correctness: PASS for equal positive widths. The archived residue-class scans cap surplus words, clear on unknown tokens and evict just one word after a match to admit overlaps. Output can be grouped by residue: the print demo for aaaaa with [aa] shows sorted expectations, but [0, 2, 1, 3] is allowed. Twelve print demos cover duplicates, swaps, overlaps, offsets, empty words list and misses. Width mismatch outside the stated contract is not validated.
concatenated-words.optimized: Slide each residue class while maintaining a multiplicity cap and number of words: O((n + B)*w) expected time, O(d*w) auxiliary space; slicing and hashing a token cost O(w).
concatenated-words.python: Slide equal-width blocks and compare entire Counter objects for each full window: O(B*w + n*(w + d)) expected time, O(B*w) auxiliary space.

contains-duplicate.contract: Return whether two distinct positions contain equal integers; empty input is false and the input is unchanged.
contains-duplicate.correctness: The Chapter2 seen-set scan is correct, including empty/singleton inputs; five printed examples, not assertions. Both guide hash/set paths are missing.
contains-duplicate.optimized: Stop at the first repeat with a seen set; expected linear worst-input time.
contains-duplicate.python: Compare len(set(values)) with len(values); consumes the full sequence.

dedupe-sorted-array.baseline: Search the written prefix before each append-to-prefix: O(n^2) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
dedupe-sorted-array.contract: For a nondecreasing integer list, write distinct values in order into its own prefix and return the prefix length. The suffix is unspecified. The lesson extends the contract to empty input.
dedupe-sorted-array.correctness: PASS within the archived nonempty bounds. The two-pointer scan correctly compares with the last retained value; it prints indices inside the function and returns 1 for the out-of-bounds empty case. Seven print demos cover equal, distinct, singleton, negative and separated duplicate runs, not empty. The guide alias has no HEAD file.
dedupe-sorted-array.optimized: Use the adjacency of equal values and compare with the last written value: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
dedupe-sorted-array.python: Use dict.fromkeys to keep first occurrences and overwrite the prefix: O(n) expected time, O(u) auxiliary space, not the strict constant-space solution.

dedupe-sorted-linked-list.baseline: Collect the nodes, select the first node of each run, then relink only those nodes. This explicitly picks a policy and uses linear auxiliary space.
dedupe-sorted-linked-list.contract: From a sorted acyclic chain, relink one existing node for each equal-value run. The original value-only contract does not specify which duplicate survives.
dedupe-sorted-linked-list.correctness: Iterative splicing keeps the first node in each run, while recursive suffix deduplication keeps the last; both produce correct values, but identity is different. Iteration's printed cases cover empty/singleton, distinct, all-equal and repeated boundary runs. The single recursive sample checks only values; neither enforces an identity policy.
dedupe-sorted-linked-list.optimized: Skip duplicate successors without advancing the retained node. This yields O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space versus O(n) recursive frames for the archived suffix solution.
dedupe-sorted-linked-list.python: itertools.groupby groups adjacent equal values on an already sorted input. Promptly take each group's first node, then relink those selections without allocating replacement nodes.

design-hashmap.contract: Put overwrites, remove of a missing key does nothing, and get returns -1 when absent; no built-in hash table. Archive keys/values are nonnegative and at most one million, with at most ten thousand calls.
design-hashmap.correctness: Both fixed chaining variants work, but average cost depends on load and distribution. The fixed open-addressing probe terminates under the archive operation cap; beyond it, a table with no never-used slot can loop even with tombstones. Printed demos cover insert/update/delete; linked chaining has explicit collisions, not the probing demo.
design-hashmap.optimized: Rehash chained entries when occupancy grows; adversarial collisions can still cause linear operations.
design-hashmap.python: No compliant built-in; partition tuple pairs into list buckets.

first-unique-character.baseline: Use a fresh count for each candidate.
first-unique-character.contract: Return the earliest index whose case-sensitive character occurs exactly once, or -1; indices are Python character positions.
first-unique-character.correctness: Chapter2 frequency, Counter and first-index tracking agree; its examples are printed. The string companion verifies frequency and OrderedDict variants with empty, none and late matches. The differently named strings alias and dictionary lookup link have no file.
first-unique-character.optimized: Record first positions in insertion order and mark repeats; only scan distinct keys after ingesting the text.
first-unique-character.python: Count once with Counter and look up indices in order.

four-sum.baseline: Enumerate all increasing index quadruples and deduplicate matching sorted values: O(n^4) time, O(r) auxiliary space excluding r returned quadruplets.
four-sum.contract: Return distinct value quadruplets totaling the target, each realized at four different input positions; order of quadruplets is immaterial.
four-sum.correctness: PASS. The archived sort mutates the input; anchor and endpoint duplicate skips make each value quadruplet unique even when different positions hold the same value. Thirteen print demos include duplicate-heavy, signed, empty and too-short inputs; demo 11 gives four of the seven valid quadruplets, and demo 13 lists two impossible quadruplets needing a second zero. Python arithmetic does not overflow fixed-width sums.
four-sum.optimized: Sort a copy, fix two anchors, and scan the suffix from both ends: O(n log n + n^3) time, O(n) auxiliary space including the copy and sorting scratch.
four-sum.python: Counter and combinations_with_replacement enumerate d distinct values, checking multiplicity: expected O(n + d log d + d^4) time, O(d) auxiliary space.

four-sum-count.contract: Count index tuples taking exactly one value from each list; duplicates multiply the count and an empty input list yields zero.
four-sum-count.correctness: Original flat and verbose pair-frequency maps, Counter and four nested loops are correct. Printed examples cover repeat multiplicity and zero solutions, but do not assert agreement across every variant. Guide lookup alias is missing.
four-sum-count.optimized: Count each input first and multiply occurrence weights over distinct-value pairs, reducing work on repeated values.
four-sum-count.python: Use Counter over all sums on one side, then look up each opposite sum.

generate-parentheses.baseline: No exhaustive two-choice search is implemented.
generate-parentheses.contract: For a small nonnegative n, return all well-formed strings of n pairs in lexicographic order, including [""] at n=0.
generate-parentheses.correctness: The archive prunes prefixes with too many closes or opens and its empty case is a singleton empty arrangement, not an empty list.
generate-parentheses.python: No direct built-in; combinations can enumerate candidate open positions.

group-anagrams.baseline: Compare each word's counts with representative signatures of existing groups.
group-anagrams.contract: Group strings by character multiset; preserve occurrences, including duplicate words and empty strings. Bucket order is immaterial.
group-anagrams.correctness: Sorted signatures support arbitrary case-sensitive characters. The 26-bin and distinct-prime product variants are correct on lowercase ASCII only (negative indices can silently alias for out-of-domain letters); prime multiplication uses growing integers. Demos are printed; both extra guide aliases are missing.
group-anagrams.optimized: Use an unordered, hashable frequency signature for all characters; a fixed array is appropriate only with a specified alphabet.
group-anagrams.python: Use a sorted character tuple as a defaultdict key.

happy-number.baseline: Both set variants do arithmetic digit extraction and remember visited states. Charge space per distinct state and digit work per transition.
happy-number.contract: For a positive integer in the signed 32-bit range, return whether repeated base-10 sums of squared digits reach 1. Seeing another state twice implies a cycle.
happy-number.correctness: Both chapters' set and Floyd variants are correct on the contract. Chapter 4's 1-or-4 shortcut is also correct on that domain, but hangs for zero or negatives, which are outside it. Its sequence helper is a bounded diagnostic, not another boolean solver; it appends the terminal 1 or repeated state after a step. Chapter 2 prints happy/unhappy/fixed-point samples; Chapter 4 adds the cycle sentinel, a power of ten and sequences, but not the upper bound. These are print checks.
happy-number.optimized: Both Floyd versions use constant state for this bounded integer domain and need no knowledge of the nonhappy cycle. Do not equate the digit count with the number of transitions.
happy-number.python: No direct classifier in the stdlib. A sum over decimal characters makes the transition readable for the documented small integers; a 1-or-4 stop is specific to this digit rule.

isomorphic-strings.baseline: Compare equality relationships between all pairs of positions.
isomorphic-strings.contract: Return whether equally long strings are connected by a bijection on characters, or false if their lengths differ.
isomorphic-strings.correctness: Original dual dictionaries enforce both directions but zip silently truncates unequal lengths; for example empty versus nonempty incorrectly passes. Assertions cover equal-length success/conflicts and both-empty only. The guide alias resolves to this same file.
isomorphic-strings.optimized: Check mappings or last-seen positions in lockstep after an explicit length guard.

jewels-and-stones.baseline: Check each stone against the jewel string.
jewels-and-stones.contract: Count stone occurrences whose case-sensitive type is a jewel; prize membership is not multiplicative.
jewels-and-stones.correctness: All three Chapter2 methods return the same results. The purported one-liner rebuilds the jewel set for each stone; the other two build it once and otherwise duplicate the strategy. Coverage is printed examples, including case sensitivity.
jewels-and-stones.optimized: For a fixed jewel alphabet, use a small membership mask or constant-space lookup; for arbitrary strings use the set rather than rebuilding it.
jewels-and-stones.python: Build one set, then count matching occurrences with sum.

lfu-cache.baseline: Store frequency and access timestamp, scanning for the victim.
lfu-cache.contract: A get hit or overwrite counts as an access; insertions start at frequency one, misses return -1, and eviction uses lowest frequency then oldest access. Capacity zero is valid.
lfu-cache.correctness: Both linked-bucket and OrderedDict-bucket archive variants maintain minimum frequency and recency correctly. Linked assertions cover LFU, tied LRU, zero and one capacity; OrderedDict gets a shorter trace. Neither original trace asserts overwrite behavior.
lfu-cache.optimized: Splice nodes in per-frequency doubly linked queues; expected amortized constant operations under standard dictionary assumptions.
lfu-cache.python: Use each OrderedDict as an LRU bucket, with a tracked minimum frequency.

linked-cycle.baseline: Keep visited nodes in a list and scan by identity at each step. This makes the recurrence criterion explicit but costs quadratic time.
linked-cycle.contract: Return whether following next links from a possibly empty head revisits the same node; do not mutate links or confuse duplicate values with a cycle.
linked-cycle.correctness: Both chapters' Floyd and set variants are correct for their identity-equality/hash classes. Chapter 3 prints two cyclic and empty/singleton cases plus both outcomes for the set; Chapter 4 adds a self-loop and a longer stem. Neither tests equal-valued distinct nodes or asserts that links are unchanged.
linked-cycle.optimized: Floyd uses two speeds and checks identity after advancing; it uses O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
linked-cycle.python: The originals' visited set is the direct Python helper. It uses expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space, where n is the number of reachable nodes.

linked-intersection.baseline: Compare each candidate from A against the nodes in B by identity; O(mn) worst-case time, constant auxiliary space.
linked-intersection.contract: Return the first shared node by identity for two acyclic chains; leave both unchanged. Matching values do not count, and absent intersection returns None.
linked-intersection.correctness: Head switching, a set of nodes and length alignment are correct with the archived identity-equality/hash ListNode. Prefer explicit identity tests for comparisons; hash keys must also preserve identity. The sample builder prepends an unintended extra node for skip_a or skip_b equal to zero; its zero-value sentinel is only a fixture convention. Printed cases cover shared suffixes and disjoint inputs but not equal-valued disjoint chains or a shared head.
linked-intersection.optimized: Original head switching and length alignment both use O(m+n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Switching equalizes the unshared prefixes without a counting pass.
linked-intersection.python: The original set approach is idiomatic on the supplied class. An identity-key set can remove any dependence on node equality or hash overrides.

longest-common-subsequence.baseline: No exhaustive subsequence reference is implemented.
longest-common-subsequence.contract: Return the longest shared subsequence length, which does not require adjacent characters; empty input gives 0.
longest-common-subsequence.correctness: The archive uses the correct recurrence and puts the shorter string on the row axis; it allocates a fresh row at every outer step.
longest-common-subsequence.optimized: Rolling rows give O(min(m, n) + 1) auxiliary space.
longest-common-subsequence.python: No direct standard-library equivalent; a full tabulation can expose the recurrence.

longest-consecutive.baseline: Check list membership while extending from candidate starts.
longest-consecutive.contract: Return the longest run of adjacent integer values, without relying on input order; duplicates do not extend a run.
longest-consecutive.correctness: Original set-start, verbose, sorting and union-find versions are correct. Sorting also appears in verbose, so it misses the linear target; union-find has inverse-Ackermann amortized cost and recursive find. Printed cases cover negatives, duplicates, empty and singleton; both guide aliases are missing.
longest-consecutive.optimized: Use a set and only walk runs from values with no predecessor.
longest-consecutive.python: Sort the distinct values, then count adjacent streaks.

longest-duplicate-substring.baseline: Compare pairs of suffix starts by walking their common prefix.
longest-duplicate-substring.contract: Return any longest repeated substring, allowing overlaps, or the empty string if none exists.
longest-duplicate-substring.correctness: Archive hash candidates are verified exactly; the lowercase base can collide more outside that alphabet. Slice-set search can take cubic time and quadratic storage; sorted suffix copies use quadratic storage. Tests exercise overlap and compare rolling hash/suffix lengths on five cases; the long case checks only nonemptiness and the slice-set method is not exercised.
longest-duplicate-substring.optimized: Build suffix ranks by doubling, then scan adjacent LCPs in linear time; avoids collision-dependent bounds and full suffix copies.
longest-duplicate-substring.python: Sort suffix strings and compare adjacent suffixes; materializing them copies a quadratic number of characters.

longest-k-distinct.baseline: Grow each candidate from its own start and stop at k+1 distinct values: expected O(n^2) time, O(min(d, k+1)) auxiliary space for k > 0.
longest-k-distinct.contract: Return the longest contiguous string length using at most k distinct code points; empty input or k <= 0 returns zero.
longest-k-distinct.correctness: PASS. The archived counts delete zero-frequency entries so len(counts) is the distinct count; the left boundary advances until the budget holds. Five assertions cover mixed letters, repeated letters, empty, k=0 and k beyond the alphabet seen, not negative k though the guard handles it. The guide path aliases this tracked source.
longest-k-distinct.optimized: Maintain only live frequencies and shrink as soon as the distinct limit is exceeded: expected O(n) time and O(min(d, k+1)) auxiliary space for k > 0.
longest-k-distinct.python: Use OrderedDict of last positions and evict the least recent key to jump the left boundary: expected O(n) time, O(min(d, k+1)) auxiliary space for k > 0.

longest-palindromic-substring.contract: Return the leftmost longest contiguous palindrome, or the empty string for empty input.
longest-palindromic-substring.correctness: The archive expands odd and even centers left to right with strict best-length updates, preserving the leftmost tie. This is center expansion, not table-based DP.
longest-palindromic-substring.optimized: Center expansion runs in O(n^2) time with constant auxiliary space. Linear-time Manacher is not implemented.
longest-palindromic-substring.python: No direct built-in; slicing can check candidates with a simpler expression.

longest-unique-substring.baseline: Extend a candidate per starting point and search the already-included substring for repeats: O(n^3) time, O(n) slice space.
longest-unique-substring.contract: Return the length of the longest contiguous string segment with distinct characters; spaces count, and empty returns zero. The first two archived variants and the lesson support arbitrary Python string code points.
longest-unique-substring.correctness: PASS. The primary set window shrinks through a duplicate; the last-index variant only advances past occurrences inside the window; the direct-address variant is ASCII-only and raises IndexError for code points at least 128. Seven print demos cover the primary version and three ASCII demos per alternate. The spaced example claims 4, but the true answer is 3. Both guide aliases have no HEAD source.
longest-unique-substring.optimized: Jump the left edge forward using each character's last index: expected O(n) time and O(d) auxiliary space.
longest-unique-substring.python: Use a fresh set for each starting point to avoid rescanning its previous characters: expected O(n^2) time and O(d) auxiliary space.

max-average-window.baseline: Recompute each exact-width sum using indices: O((n-k+1)*k) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
max-average-window.contract: Return the maximum average across nonempty contiguous windows of exactly k entries for 1 <= k <= len(nums), including negative values.
max-average-window.correctness: PASS for both variants on valid widths. The main rolling sum initializes via an O(k) slice; the verbose version starts with indexed addition, retains the earliest best window, then slices for display except when k equals n. Neither is strictly O(1) auxiliary over the full operation as written. Five print demos cover ordinary, equal, negative, singleton and full-width inputs; one executes the verbose variant. The guide alias has no HEAD file.
max-average-window.optimized: Initialize without slicing and exchange outgoing and incoming integers; divide once: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
max-average-window.python: Build prefix totals using itertools.accumulate, then subtract adjacent-width bounds: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

max-vowels-window.baseline: Count vowels afresh for each window using indices: O((n-k+1)*k) time for k > 0, O(1) auxiliary space.
max-vowels-window.contract: Maximize the count of vowels in an exact-width substring. Chapter5's domain is lowercase English; the strings variant counts ASCII vowels case-insensitively and accepts empty with k=0. The lesson uses the case-insensitive ASCII-vowel rule and 0 <= k <= len(text).
max-vowels-window.correctness: PASS. Chapter5 provides a rolling count with early exit, a rolling variant returning (count, substring, earliest index), and a sliced brute-force count. There are six count print demos, one positions demo and one brute/rolling cross-check. The strings rolling variant has six assertions including mixed case and empty width; both rolling sources slice the initial window. Neither source validates oversized k. The strings guide path aliases the second tracked source.
max-vowels-window.optimized: Use a rolling count without copies; stop when the count reaches k: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
max-vowels-window.python: Use itertools.accumulate for vowel prefix counts: O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.

max-water-container.baseline: Evaluate every pair: O(n^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
max-water-container.contract: For nonnegative line heights at consecutive indices, maximize width times the shorter endpoint height; interior heights do not affect a pair. The lesson returns zero for fewer than two lines.
max-water-container.correctness: PASS. Moving the shorter endpoint rules out only narrower pairs that it would still bound; either side may move on a tie. Eight print demos cover two lines, plateaus, equally tall ends and an interior optimum; no zero-height or short input demo beyond a pair. The guide alias has no HEAD file.
max-water-container.optimized: Evaluate outside-in and move the shorter endpoint: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
max-water-container.python: Sort indices by descending height, tracking the extremes among eligible lines at each height threshold: O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

merge-sorted-linked-lists.baseline: Materializing inputs then stable-sorting their node references is correct if the output links reuse those same nodes. It needs linear auxiliary space.
merge-sorted-linked-lists.contract: Merge two disjoint, acyclic, nondecreasing chains by splicing original nodes. Keep duplicates. Both originals choose the left input first on ties.
merge-sorted-linked-lists.correctness: Iterative and recursive merges are correct under these preconditions. Sharing a nonempty suffix can produce a cycle in the iterative method; these are not alias-safe merges. The printed iterative samples cover empty inputs, ties and a remaining tail; recursion is shown once on interleaving inputs. None check node reuse or tie order by identity.
merge-sorted-linked-lists.optimized: Iterative two-head splicing is linear worst-case and constant auxiliary space. Recursive splicing has linear worst-case frames; the original short input bound keeps it practical.
merge-sorted-linked-lists.python: heapq.merge can lazily merge two node iterators using a value key, but it does not splice links itself. Capture each successor before yielding its node.

middle-linked-list.baseline: Count all nodes and walk to the chosen index. This is linear time with constant auxiliary space and makes the convention explicit.
middle-linked-list.contract: Return the original center node of an acyclic chain; pick the second middle by default and distinguish first-middle behavior for even lengths. Treat an empty extension as returning None.
middle-linked-list.correctness: Both chapters' count-and-walk and main fast/slow variants correctly return the second middle; Chapter 4 adds a correct first-middle variant. Chapter 3's array variant indexes an empty list (outside its documented nonempty domain); Chapter 4 guards it. Both print odd/even/singleton cases; Chapter 4 prints first-middle and more lengths but does not exercise empty input.
middle-linked-list.optimized: Two speeds find either middle in one pass and constant auxiliary space. Starting fast one node ahead selects the first middle; starting both at the head selects the second.
middle-linked-list.python: The array variants use list indexing after collecting references. Guard the empty case if supported and index nodes, not a copied value list.

minimum-score-spread.baseline: No exhaustive subset reference is implemented.
minimum-score-spread.contract: For 1 <= k <= len(scores), return the smallest maximum-minus-minimum among exactly k positions, without mutating scores in the worked edition.
minimum-score-spread.correctness: The endpoint scan is correct, but the original mutates its input and prints debug output. The verbose alternative copies and slices each window and is O(n log n + nk); sorting itself can use linear auxiliary storage.
minimum-score-spread.optimized: The main original implementation uses indexed endpoints after sorting.
minimum-score-spread.python: The verbose variant uses sorted() and slices, but has debug output.

minimum-window.baseline: Extend each starting point and check all required counts until it covers: expected O(m + n^2*d) time, O(d) auxiliary space.
minimum-window.contract: Return the shortest case-sensitive contiguous source substring covering every target occurrence, not merely distinct characters; return empty for an empty target or impossible cover. The lesson breaks equal-length ties by earliest start.
minimum-window.correctness: PASS for the Chapter1 and strings/sliding_window variants. Both count covered character types, not raw distinct window characters, and keep the first equal-length answer. Chapter1 takes a slice on every improvement, potentially quadratic time from copying, and has 14 print demos; the strings variant records bounds and slices once, with seven assertions including empty target and duplicates. Both keep count-map keys for irrelevant source characters. The strings guide path aliases the second tracked source.
minimum-window.optimized: Track outstanding required occurrences by threshold crossings; save indices and slice once: expected O(n + m) time, O(d) auxiliary space.
minimum-window.python: Use Counter subtraction for a readability-first sliding cover test: expected O(m + n*d) time, O(d) auxiliary space.

move-zeroes.baseline: Repeatedly remove an encountered zero and append it, processing exactly n original entries: O(n^2) time, O(1) algorithmic auxiliary space.
move-zeroes.contract: Mutate the original integer list in place, stably moving all zeroes after the nonzeroes; return None. No extra full list in the strict solution.
move-zeroes.correctness: PASS. The archived scan swaps the next encountered nonzero into the first hole, preserves nonzero order, and runs in O(n) time/O(1) auxiliary space. Its 12 print demos cover singletons, all/none/mixed zeroes and negatives; demo 12 declares the wrong expected list for [1, 0, 2]. The separate guide alias has no HEAD file.
move-zeroes.optimized: Compact nonzero entries with a read and write index, then fill the suffix with zeroes: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
move-zeroes.python: Stable list.sort by the zero predicate: same result and list identity, O(n log n) time and O(n) scratch, so not the strict space solution.

nearby-duplicate.baseline: Compare only pairs within the distance limit: O(n*min(n, k) + n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
nearby-duplicate.contract: Check for two distinct equal-valued positions whose index difference is at most k, for k >= 0. The archive also has a different API returning all qualifying pairs.
nearby-duplicate.correctness: PASS for three archived variants with nonnegative k. The bounded set checks before inserting and retains exactly the eligible prior positions; the last-index map checks the closest prior match. Pair enumeration is correct but scans every earlier equal index, with O(n^2) worst-case time even if few pairs qualify, plus O(n) bookkeeping. Six print demos cover the set, one the map and one pair enumeration, including boundary and k=0 cases. The set guide alias has no HEAD file.
nearby-duplicate.optimized: Bound the set to the last k positions before each membership check: O(n) expected time, O(min(n, k)) auxiliary space for k > 0.
nearby-duplicate.python: Use dict.get to retrieve the latest prior position: O(n) expected time and O(d) auxiliary space.

next-greater-element.baseline: Find the query position and scan to the first qualifying successor. O(qn) worst-case time, constant auxiliary space excluding output.
next-greater-element.contract: For each query value, find the first strictly larger value to its right in the reference array, or -1. Reference values are distinct and every query is present; preserve query order.
next-greater-element.correctness: The original brute-force and monotone-stack variants both meet the uniqueness/presence assumptions. On duplicate reference values the first occurrence chosen by index need not agree with the value-keyed precomputation, so duplicate support would need a location-based query. Only the stack is exercised in the four printed comparisons (mixed, increasing, delayed greater, singleton).
next-greater-element.optimized: Resolve pending values when a strictly larger value arrives. Each value enters and leaves the stack at most once; expected O(n+q) time and O(n) auxiliary space with hash maps.
next-greater-element.python: Build an index dictionary once, then use next with a default over candidate positions. It avoids repeated position lookups but does not remove worst-case suffix scanning.

palindrome-buildable.baseline: No explicit pair matching is implemented.
palindrome-buildable.contract: Return the maximum length when any multiset of characters can be rearranged, with case significant.
palindrome-buildable.correctness: Pair counts and at most one odd center are correct. A stale TODO is next to the completed implementation.
palindrome-buildable.optimized: The frequency-map solution is already expected linear; a parity set can avoid storing exact counts.
palindrome-buildable.python: The original counts manually rather than using Counter.

palindrome-linked-list.baseline: Chapter 4's half-stack compares the second half against stored values. It takes O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space; recursion also consumes linear frames.
palindrome-linked-list.contract: Compare values in an acyclic chain against their reverse without leaving changed links. A constant-space implementation may reverse a suffix temporarily if exclusive access is available.
palindrome-linked-list.correctness: Both chapters' array, recursive and restoring half-reversal variants are correct on recursion-safe inputs; the recursive solver cannot handle the full 100,000-node limit in standard Python. Chapter 4's half-stack solver is correct for odd and even lengths. Printed coverage spans both parities, singleton and mismatches; Chapter 4 prints one successful restoration by value, not node identity or restoration after a mismatch. Empty input works in all variants but is not sampled.
palindrome-linked-list.optimized: Both chapters' two-speed split, reverse, compare and restore use O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Preserve the reversed-half head, even when the comparison stops early.
palindrome-linked-list.python: Materialize the values and compare with a reverse slice (another linear allocation), or compare views using reversed. Do not compare node identities for this exercise.

partition-labels.baseline: No repeated cut validation is implemented.
partition-labels.contract: Return the lengths of the maximum number of contiguous parts with no character shared across parts.
partition-labels.correctness: The last-occurrence scan closes each part at the earliest safe boundary. Its O(1) auxiliary space applies to a fixed alphabet; otherwise the map uses O(u) space.
partition-labels.optimized: The last-occurrence greedy scan is implemented.
partition-labels.python: No set.isdisjoint cut-checking example is implemented.

phone-letter-combinations.baseline: No breadth-first prefix materialization is implemented.
phone-letter-combinations.contract: For a short sequence of digits 2 through 9, return all strings in keypad order. Empty input returns [].
phone-letter-combinations.correctness: The archive handles repeated digits and four-letter keys; unsupported characters raise a key lookup error and are outside the contract.
phone-letter-combinations.optimized: Depth-first generation reuses one path with output-optimal time.

remove-linked-values.baseline: Collect matching survivors as node references, then rewire and terminate the new tail. This separates deciding which nodes stay from changing links.
remove-linked-values.contract: Return the possibly changed head after removing every matching node from an acyclic chain. Keep original surviving nodes in order; an emptied list returns None.
remove-linked-values.correctness: Sentinel, manual leading-run removal and recursive filtering are correct on value/order; recursion is not safe at the documented 10,000-node limit. The recursive version can modify links on removed nodes, so don't assume removed nodes are detached. The sentinel demos print empty, all-match, head/tail runs, absent target and singletons; the other two each print one mixed example, not identity or long input.
remove-linked-values.optimized: The original sentinel or two-stage head handling bypasses removed nodes directly, avoiding a write for every retained node. Iteration is O(n) time with constant auxiliary space.
remove-linked-values.python: No direct linked-list filter; Python's lazy filter can select nodes from a mutation-safe iterator and feed a relinking helper.

repeated-substring.baseline: Try each viable divisor of the length and verify it as a period.
repeated-substring.contract: Return true iff a nonempty string is made by repeating a shorter nonempty unit at least twice; empty and singleton are false.
repeated-substring.correctness: The original doubled-and-trimmed membership formula is correct, and asserts empty, singleton, repeated and nonrepeated examples. Doubling and trimming allocate linear-size strings.
repeated-substring.optimized: Use the longest proper prefix/suffix and require exact divisibility by the implied period.
repeated-substring.python: Search the doubled input excluding its first and last alignments.

reverse-linked-list.baseline: Repeatedly detach the remaining tail and append it to the result: O(n²) time because the list has no predecessor links, and constant auxiliary space.
reverse-linked-list.contract: Reverse next links of the original nodes of a possibly empty acyclic singly linked list; return the old tail, and terminate the new tail.
reverse-linked-list.correctness: Both original algorithms reverse links correctly when recursion completes, but the recursive variant cannot handle lists up to 5,000 on standard Python settings. Four printed samples show normal, empty and singleton iteration and a two-node recursive case; they compare values only.
reverse-linked-list.optimized: Save each successor before reversing one link. Iteration is O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; recursive unwinding needs O(n) frames.
reverse-linked-list.python: There is no direct linked-list reverse method. Materialize node references, then use reversed and relink them. Reversed iteration adds no second list, but the reference list is linear auxiliary space.

reverse-string.baseline: Build an indexed reversed buffer and overwrite the list: O(n) time/O(n) auxiliary space, only a reference for the strict space contract.
reverse-string.contract: Reverse the entries of a mutable character list in its existing storage and return None; the strict implementation must not allocate a second list.
reverse-string.correctness: PASS. Opposite-end swaps stop before crossing and are safe for empty or singleton lists. Twelve print demos cover odd/even lengths, repeats, spaces, punctuation and mixed case; empty is not shown.
reverse-string.optimized: Swap symmetric entries until reaching the center: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
reverse-string.python: list.reverse mutates the original list in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; it implements the same underlying swap idea as the explicit version.

search-insert-position.contract: Return the first index with value >= target, or the length when no such position exists.
search-insert-position.correctness: The original is correct for distinct values; it stops on an arbitrary match with duplicates, so the worked edition extends it to lower bounds with duplicates.
search-insert-position.optimized: The original searches a sorted, distinct list in logarithmic time.

short-url-codec.baseline: Store full URLs in a list and find existing aliases by a linear search.
short-url-codec.contract: Within one instance, generate stable unique aliases for distinct nonempty URLs; decode the exact issued alias or return empty for an unknown alias. No network or persistence.
short-url-codec.correctness: Random, decimal, truncated-MD5-with-suffix and base62 variants round-trip issued aliases. All use replace on decode, accepting bare or repeated prefixes; random retries are unbounded near exhaustion; counters are predictable, and MD5 is not a security guarantee. Printed demos lack forced collisions and malformed aliases.
short-url-codec.optimized: Use a reverse URL map and dense indexed storage with compact base62 aliases; validate canonical decoding.
short-url-codec.python: Use two dictionaries and decimal IDs.

simplify-path.baseline: Split on slash and track the surviving directories on a stack. Count the allocated split pieces as linear auxiliary space even when few survive.
simplify-path.contract: Lexically normalize a nonempty absolute Unix path; collapse all slash runs, clamp parents at root, ignore exact dot components, and preserve other names. Never inspect symlinks or the filesystem.
simplify-path.correctness: The archived split-and-stack solver is correct for absolute paths, including dot-like names. It returns an absolute result for relative/empty strings rather than rejecting them; the length constraint mentions zero despite the absolute-path requirement. Seven assertions cover root-only slash runs, excess parents, redundant slashes and exact dots, but not leading exactly two slashes followed by a name or literal dot-like names.
simplify-path.optimized: Scan backward and carry a count of unresolved parent steps. Skip canceled spans before slicing, keeping only the components that survive. This stays linear while avoiding storage proportional to canceled names.
simplify-path.python: Use posixpath.normpath after collapsing all leading slashes to exactly one. Raw normpath preserves exactly two leading slashes, contrary to this contract.

sort-colors.baseline: No quadratic sorting example is implemented.
sort-colors.contract: Mutate a list of 0, 1, and 2 into nondecreasing order; return None.
sort-colors.correctness: The Dutch flag loop is correct within the three-value domain. Its last branch assumes the value is 2; it is not a general sorter.
sort-colors.optimized: One pass partitions three regions with constant auxiliary space.

sorted-squares.baseline: Insert each square into the appropriate position in the output: O(n^2) time, O(1) auxiliary space excluding output.
sorted-squares.contract: Given a nondecreasing integer list, return a new nondecreasing list of every square; preserve multiplicities and do not mutate the input.
sorted-squares.correctness: PASS. The archived scan correctly fills from the right because the greatest remaining magnitude is at an endpoint, including on an absolute-value tie. Thirteen print demos cover signs, zeros, duplicate squares, extreme magnitudes and singletons, not empty. The guide alias has no HEAD file.
sorted-squares.optimized: Square the greater remaining magnitude and fill back to front: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space excluding output.
sorted-squares.python: Use sorted on a generator of squares: O(n log n) worst-case time and O(n) auxiliary sorting scratch excluding output.

sorted-two-sum.baseline: Try each increasing index pair: O(n^2) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
sorted-two-sum.contract: A nondecreasing integer list and a target have exactly one pair of distinct indices. Return those indices in increasing order and zero-based, not the values. The lesson returns None if no pair exists.
sorted-two-sum.correctness: PASS for the output contract. The archived complement map checks before storing, so it cannot reuse a position; index zero is not mistaken for absence. Despite the archived title it does not exploit sorted order and uses O(n) extra space; its no-pair result is implicit None. Five print demos cover nonadjacent pairs, negatives and index zero, not duplicate-value pairs or missing targets.
sorted-two-sum.optimized: Discard one endpoint using the ordered sums: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
sorted-two-sum.python: bisect_left locates a complement in the strict suffix: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space, no suffix copy.

string-list-codec.baseline: Append length frames to an accumulating string and scan manually.
string-list-codec.contract: Encode a list of strings losslessly, including delimiters and empties; lengths represent Python characters, not UTF-8 bytes.
string-list-codec.correctness: The original length-prefixed join and decoder round-trip valid data; its bytes wording is wrong. Tests cover empty list vs empty items, separator-like payloads and controls, but not Unicode or malformed data. Original decoder assumes well-formed input and can truncate invalid input silently or throw.
string-list-codec.optimized: Stream framed writes into StringIO and parse by cursor without slicing unconsumed suffixes.
string-list-codec.python: No dedicated standard length-frame codec; use join and offset-based str.find.

subarray-sum.contract: Count nonempty contiguous ranges that total k, allowing negative values and zero.
subarray-sum.correctness: Both original prefix-frequency versions seed zero and count before insertion; brute-force accumulates per start correctly. Examples are printed and cover negatives, zero, singleton and no match. Both guide aliases are missing.
subarray-sum.optimized: Use a compact list of counters when the observed prefix span is suitably small, otherwise fall back to a streaming dict.
subarray-sum.python: Use accumulate to generate prefix totals, with Counter for previously seen totals.

substring-search.baseline: Test candidates character by character, avoiding slice copies.
substring-search.contract: Find the first match or -1, and all starts including overlap. An empty pattern matches at all boundaries; its first match is zero.
substring-search.correctness: Easy archive slicing and both medium KMP functions are correct. The easy source understates space: substring slices can allocate O(m). Samples cover no match, empty-first, fallback and overlap; empty-all is implemented but not asserted. Exhaustive short binary strings agreed with find and startswith.
substring-search.optimized: Use KMP's border table and resume with the longest proper border after each match.
substring-search.python: Use str.find, advancing one position after a match when gathering all.

three-sum.baseline: Enumerate increasing index triples and deduplicate their sorted value tuples: O(n^3) time, O(r) auxiliary space excluding r returned triples.
three-sum.contract: Return distinct value triples totaling zero, using three different positions for each. Order of triples is immaterial.
three-sum.correctness: PASS. The archived sort mutates input; it skips repeated anchors and matched endpoint values without dropping triples that require two or three equal entries. Twelve print demos cover duplicates, all zeros, impossible signs and multiple results (some expectations only illustrative); no empty/too-short input demo. Neither guide alias has a HEAD file.
three-sum.optimized: Copy and sort, then fix one anchor and scan opposite endpoints: O(n log n + n^2) time and O(n) auxiliary space including sorting scratch.
three-sum.python: Use Counter and distinct value pairs, checking that the implied third value exists with sufficient multiplicity: O(n + d log d + d^2) expected time, O(d) auxiliary space.

top-k-frequent.baseline: Both variants that sort distinct values after counting are implemented.
top-k-frequent.contract: Return k items by decreasing frequency, breaking ties by first occurrence, for 0 <= k <= distinct count in the worked edition.
top-k-frequent.correctness: The archive assumes a unique top-k set and permits any order. The manual heap returns heap order and can choose different ties. The bucket variant misses k=0 for nonempty input, which is outside the original bounds.
top-k-frequent.optimized: Frequency buckets provide an expected linear bound.

trapping-rain.baseline: Scan both boundaries independently for each column: O(n^2) time, O(1) auxiliary space without slicing.
trapping-rain.contract: Given nonnegative heights of unit-width columns, return total trapped water; empty and fewer than three columns trap none.
trapping-rain.correctness: PASS for both archived variants. The prefix/suffix version computes strict side maxima and clamps negative contributions; the endpoint scan finalizes a side with an adequate far boundary and uses constant storage. The 15 print demos cover basins, plateaus, monotone lists and short lists but exercise only the prefix/suffix variant, not the two-pointer version. The guide alias has no HEAD file.
trapping-rain.optimized: Track side maxima and finalize the side whose known maximum is lower: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
trapping-rain.python: itertools.accumulate with max builds paired inclusive boundary sequences: O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space.

valid-anagram.contract: Compare case-sensitive character multiplicities; empty strings match and unequal lengths cannot.
valid-anagram.correctness: Chapter2 decrement-and-delete is correct and prints five examples; the string companion's signed defaultdict method is correct and asserts case/empty examples. The dictionary guide alias is missing. Constant auxiliary space requires a fixed alphabet.
valid-anagram.optimized: Maintain one table of unmatched characters and reject impossible decrements early.

valid-palindrome.baseline: Build a list of lowered characters, then compare mirrored entries: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
valid-palindrome.contract: For printable ASCII, ignore punctuation/whitespace and letter case; digits are retained. Empty normalized text is a palindrome. The lesson also accepts empty input.
valid-palindrome.correctness: PASS for archived printable ASCII. The scan skips non-alphanumeric endpoints and compares lowercase characters. Do not equate this with general Unicode case folding/normalization, where characters can expand. Eight print demos cover ignored characters, digits, mixed case, singleton and mismatches; no empty input demo. The normalized-palindrome guide alias has no HEAD file.
valid-palindrome.optimized: Skip ignored characters from the ends without making a normalized copy: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
valid-palindrome.python: Use an ASCII regular-expression filter and compare the lowercase string with its reversed slice: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

valid-parentheses.baseline: For each closer, search backward for the opener at its nesting depth. Repeated scanning uses O(n²) time but O(1) auxiliary space.
valid-parentheses.contract: Check well-nested matching for (), [] and {}. An empty string is balanced; other characters are not silently ignored.
valid-parentheses.correctness: Both archived files use the same opener-stack algorithm and are correct; a non-bracket character cannot match a valid closer and thus also forces rejection. The Chapter 7 printed cases cover crossed brackets and leading closers; the strings version uses assertions including mixed nesting and empty input, but misses those two negative cases. Neither tests deep inputs.
valid-parentheses.optimized: A single pass with an opener stack takes O(n) time and O(depth) auxiliary space. Reject a closer that does not match the top.
valid-parentheses.python: A regex can repeatedly remove adjacent matching pairs, not validate arbitrary nesting in a single ordinary Python regex. Deep inputs make the repeated rewrite quadratic.

word-pattern.baseline: Compare equality for every pair of corresponding positions.
word-pattern.contract: Words compared case-sensitively must form a bijection with pattern characters; counts must match. split() allows arbitrary whitespace.
word-pattern.correctness: The Chapter2 two-map and canonical-signature implementations and the companion two-map implementation are correct. Chapter2 prints examples; companion assertions cover both conflict directions and mismatched counts. Chapter2's single-pass name hides two signatures and their lists.
word-pattern.optimized: Check forward and reverse mappings together; reject on the first conflict.
word-pattern.python: Compare canonical patterns produced by dict-based enumeration.
